Negotiate data access contracts via the: Negotiate data access contracts via the Dataspace Protocol using ODRL policies. Select a consumer participant, choose a dataset, and initiate a contract negotiation request that the data holder can accept or reject.
Two steps: (1) choose a data provider an: Two steps: (1) choose a data provider and click Discover Offers to see what datasets are available; (2) select a dataset and click Start Negotiation to request access.

Monitor and initiate EDC-V data transfer: Monitor and initiate EDC-V data transfers via the DSP Transfer Process (Signalling Protocol). Once a contract is agreed, start a transfer to pull FHIR or OMOP data from the provider's data plane.
The DSP Signalling Protocol defines the: The DSP Signalling Protocol defines the transfer state machine: REQUESTED → STARTED → COMPLETED (or TERMINATED on failure). Each transfer is secured by EDC-V access tokens issued during the STARTED phase.
No transfer processes yet. Start one fro: No transfer processes yet. Start one from an agreed contract above.

No finalized agreements found. Complete: No finalized agreements found. Complete a contract negotiation first.
Track all DSP protocol tasks across your: Track all DSP protocol tasks across your dataspace participants. Negotiations and transfers are shown as live state pipelines following the Dataspace Protocol and Data Plane Signaling (DPS) specification.
Negotiations and transfers for {org}. Us: Negotiations and transfers for {org}. Use action buttons to advance the DSP state machine.
Tasks are aggregated from all registered: Tasks are aggregated from all registered participant contexts. Negotiations follow: REQUESTED → OFFERED → ACCEPTED → AGREED → VERIFIED → FINALIZED. Transfers follow: REQUESTED → STARTED → SUSPENDED → COMPLETED. The EDR badge indicates the Data Plane has been signalled via DPS and generated an Endpoint Data Reference with JWT bearer token.
The connector's management API is not an: The connector's management API is not answering{detail}. These are the tasks the hub last synced to its store; they may be stale.
No tasks yet. Start by sharing data or n: No tasks yet. Start by sharing data or negotiating a contract.
Layer 4: OMOP CDM cohort statistics from: Layer 4: OMOP CDM cohort statistics from the Synthea-generated dataset, supporting EHDS Art. 53 secondary-use research. View aggregate counts for persons, conditions, drugs, measurements, and procedures.
Analytics are computed from OMOP CDM nod: Analytics are computed from OMOP CDM nodes in Neo4j. The OMOP Common Data Model standardises clinical data across institutions, enabling federated cohort analysis without moving patient-level data.
Ask questions about the Health Dataspace: Ask questions about the Health Dataspace knowledge graph in plain language. The query engine translates your question into Cypher and returns structured results from all five graph layers.

One secure processing environment return: One secure processing environment returned fewer than {k} records, so the whole answer is withheld: a missing contributor would identify people.
Counts below {k} are shown as <{k}, and: Counts below {k} are shown as <{k}, and a share computed from one goes with it, so no one can be singled out (k-anonymity).
The EHDS dataspace knowledge graph is bu: The EHDS dataspace knowledge graph is built from five stacked layers. This breadcrumb shows which layers the generated Cypher reads from to answer your question.
Share of Condition nodes with a CODED_BY: Share of Condition nodes with a CODED_BY SnomedConcept link, and MedicationRequest nodes with a CODED_BY RxNormConcept link. High coverage means the cohort filter is reliable.
Lucene relevance score: higher means the: Lucene relevance score: higher means the node's indexed text matched the query terms more strongly. Not a statistical frequency.
